cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: What Was the Plan?
cards.instruction: Find out what was promised, scheduled, or changed without revealing that you lost track.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. What time did we settle on for Mum's birthday dinner? I'm checking the invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Seven, in the private room. You booked it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Right. How have you written the restaurant name? I want everything consistent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't written anything. You're doing the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then could you proofread the booking confirmation aloud? I'll type straight from you so we don't introduce any errors.

mechanism: A disguises forgotten event details as a pupil consistency and proofreading exercise.
confusable: Unlike general information probing, the specific purpose is recovering a schedule A was responsible for while pretending it is checking B work.
comparison: Event details extracted through dictation versus route recovered through a practice briefing.
seedUse: Keep D30 invitations/time/restaurant/confirmation chain; S05 taught proofreading gives a concrete pretext for asking already-known-to-organizer facts.
